primitives.name: Exponential Frequency Fit
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model - For each year, fit the lower-95% player HR counts with an exponential curve N → b·e^(-rN) (r = rate parameter, b = scale; Figure 1 caption gives the form).
primitives.assumptions: Stationarity of player performance distribution over time, valid fit of lower 95% of data with exponential decay.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When player populations deviate significantly from stationary distribution or when extreme outliers skew the fit.

primitives.name: Tail Rarity Quantification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Extrapolate the tail: a performance's annual/all-time rarity = its deviation from the year's exponential (e.g., 2005 distribution implies 1/3 of a player hits 51 HR → Andruw Jones's 51 = once-in-3-year event; Bonds 73 (2001) = once-in-10-year event; Ruth 60 (1927) = once-in-10,000-year event).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R(N)': 'rarity of N home runs (dimensionless)', 'f(N)': 'frequency of N home runs (year\\(^{-1}\\))'}
primitives.assumptions: The exponential model accurately describes the tail behavior of home run distributions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When observed frequencies diverge from exponential decay due to non-stationary or anomalous performance trends.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core methodology models annual MLB home run totals using an exponential frequency distribution \( f(N) = b \cdot e^{-rN} \), where \( N \) denotes home runs. This is inspired by the Gutenberg-Richter law for earthquake magnitudes. The model fits the lower 95% of player data to estimate \( r \) and \( b \). Tail rarity is then computed as \( R(N) = 1/f(N) \), representing how rare a performance is relative to the population. Record forecasting assumes linear drift in \( r \) and \( b \) post-1948, allowing projection of future probabilities. The model fails due to unvalidated stationarity and falsified predictions (e.g., Bonds's 73 HR record). It lacks validation through backtesting or comparison. The framework is mathematically elegant but fails in real-world application due to assumption violations and lack of robustness. The model's dual nature—descriptive and predictive—is flawed by its reliance on static assumptions and absence of empirical feedback loops.
